model.name: Every Task is reciprocated by exactly one Sprint — 109 orphans re-homed honestly, never fabricated
model.description: Measured while validating R40.49: of 525 Tasks, 109 are ORPHANS — claimed by NO Sprint at all (in zero Sprint.tasks[]) = ~20.8% of the board, invisible in sprint grouping. Breakdown (measured): 99 are old-schema (Sprint only in ownerIor, unreciprocated) = R40.49's Case-D set; +10 are non-old-schema (9 null-owner whose model.parent Sprint does NOT list them back + 1 dual-carrier 708ec0a5) = tasks that ALREADY carry an UNRECIPROCATED parent (the drawer-says-parent-X-but-overview-unsorted drift). PRE-EXISTING, surfaced by the audit, NOT caused by our work. Each Task must be reciprocated by exactly one Sprint; the 99 (and the +10) must be RE-HOMED honestly, never by fabricating a link.

measured.by: robbin-req (reproduces the D=99, adds the +10 graph-wide)

model.crossRefNote: Surfaced by the R40.49 reciprocation audit (D=99 orphans). R40.51 is graph-wide (109) = the 99 old-schema + 10 non-old-schema tasks whose parent is not reciprocated. R40.49 explicitly does NOT re-home orphans (leaves them unsorted); R40.51 owns the re-homing.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every ior:class:Task is claimed by EXACTLY ONE Sprint via Sprint.tasks[], reciprocated (the task and the Sprint agree). No task in zero sprints; none in multiple.

A detector reports the orphan count GRAPH-WIDE (tasks in zero Sprint.tasks[]) + any multi-listed. Measured now: 109 orphans of 525 (20.8%) = 99 old-schema (R40.49 Case-D) + 10 non-old-schema with an unreciprocated parent; 0 multi-listed. The detector counts all 109, not only the 99 old-schema.
The orphans are re-homed by an EXPLICIT decision path: (a) sprint-number embedded in the task name/slug, else (b) createdAt era, else (c) FLAGGED FOR TRON where genuinely unknowable. NO silent guess.

A migration must NEVER fabricate a link to satisfy its own rule. Setting a task model.parent (or ownerIor) to a Sprint whose tasks[] does not list it invents data so a migration looks complete = the exact drift this req removes. An orphan stays honestly UNSORTED until a RECIPROCATED claim exists on BOTH sides. stub-must-fail: a re-home that sets a Sprint pointer without adding the task to that Sprint.tasks[] (unreciprocated) => RED.

Recorded as PRE-EXISTING (audit-surfaced, not caused by the ownership backfill). R40.49 explicitly does NOT re-home orphans — it sets their owner + drops the stale pointer and leaves them unsorted; R40.51 does the honest re-homing separately.
